newsitem.title: INDIA: Profit-taking cuts recent gains in Indian cotton.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking cuts recent gains in Indian cotton.

text.p: Cotton prices lost some of its recent gains on Wednesday, dealers said.
Sluggish mill buying at the improved level triggered light profit-taking by stockists, dealers said.
New crop arrivals were low due to severe cold weather in the producing centres but inflow in the local market improved as state-owned agencies stepped up despatches, they said.
In the spot deals Bengal-deshi slid by 5/20 rupees to 820/865 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned fell by 5/10 rupees to 1,420/1,640 rupees per maund.
Gujarat cotton was steady in a narrow price band.
